function_question: How does nature grab and hold things of different shapes?

opening.text: There was a boy called Mateo who spent every Saturday baking with his Grandma Rosa in her cosy kitchen.
Every Saturday, Grandma dropped something: a spoon, a tea towel, her glasses case. And every time, Mateo picked it up for her.
One Saturday, Grandma sighed. "My knees are so sore, and I hate asking for help all week when you're not here."

card.problem: Grandma can't pick things up from the floor
card.goal: A grabber that picks up 5 different objects

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Too far to reach
chapters.line: Mateo wonders: how can Grandma pick things up without bending?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Mateo needs a helper
chapters.line: A helping hand needs two kind inventors. Will you join Mateo?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Mateo meet heroes that grab things of every shape.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of wrap, pinch or stick
chapters.line: The heroes share their three ways to hold on.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The grip lab
chapters.line: Mateo hands you two rulers and a pile of rubber bands.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The question for Grandma
chapters.line: Before you design, find out who it's for and what they really need.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great grabber starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The pick-up game
chapters.line: The ball keeps slipping out. You fix it, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: A helping hand
chapters.line: Grandma picks up her own glasses case and smiles.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Grandma Rosa's knees are sore, and she can't pick things up from the floor. Can you help Mateo build her a helping hand? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some inventors already have a spark of an idea for reaching the floor. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been grabbing and gripping for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes with amazing grips!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which grabber tip will pick up the most objects?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your grabber from the handle to the tips, like a real inventor!
guide.build_and_test: Build your grabber and play the pick-up game. How many of the 5 objects can you grab in 1 minute?
guide.retry_tip: Inventors never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and play the pick-up game again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Grandma Rosa keeps YOUR grabber by the kitchen door, and she picks up everything she drops all by herself.

quick_check.question: Mateo picks up all 5 objects in exactly 1 minute. On average, how many seconds did each object take?
quick_check.right: Right! 60 seconds shared between 5 objects is 12 seconds each.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. 1 minute is 60 seconds. Try 60 divided by 5.

clue_cards.name: Elephant
clue_cards.trick: A boneless trunk with a finger-like tip.
clue_cards.does: It curls round a log or pinches a single peanut.

clue_cards.name: Octopus
clue_cards.trick: Bendy arms with hundreds of suckers.
clue_cards.does: They wrap round any shape and hold on tight.

clue_cards.name: Chameleon
clue_cards.trick: A super-fast tongue with a sticky tip.
clue_cards.does: It sticks to an insect and pulls it back in a flash.

clue_cards.name: Parrot
clue_cards.trick: A hooked beak and two toes forward, two back.
clue_cards.does: It pinches tiny seeds and grips branches.

predict.prompt: Pinch it or wrap around it? Predict first!
predict.explain: Small, thin things are easiest to pinch between two tips. Big round things slip out of a pinch, so it's better to wrap around them.

lab.title: The grip lab
lab.predict: Which grabber tip will pick up the most of the 5 objects?

tool.name: How Might We
tool.intro: How Might We turns what you learn about a person into a question you can design for. It has 4 parts: User, Need, Insight and How might we…? Today you'll learn the first 2: User and Need.

parts.name: User
parts.what: Who are you designing for? Describe them in a few words.
parts.example: 🎒 A 6-year-old who walks to school with lots of books.
parts.starter: My user is Grandma Rosa, who…

parts.name: Need
parts.what: What does that person need to be able to do? Use a doing word.
parts.example: 🎒 They need to carry their books without sore shoulders.
parts.starter: Grandma Rosa needs a way to…

sketch_checklist: I drew my grabber from the handle to the tips.
I labelled how it opens and closes and what the tips are made of.
I wrote how long it is.

test.measure: objects picked up out of 5 in 1 minute
test.check_question: Grandma check: could you use it while standing up straight?
check_options: No, I had to bend down

reflection.question: Which nature trick gave your grabber its grip?
